source_title: Gemini’s latest integration can tell you if you’re getting faster, one run at a time
source_excerpt:

Strava subscribers can now connect their accounts to Google Gemini for personalized fitness and training insights.
Gemini can analyze race performance, compare personal records, track activity streaks, and assess how weather affects workouts.
The integration is read-only and rolling out in the US, with no confirmed availability date for other markets.
Strava is bringing its fitness-tracking data to Google Gemini , allowing subscribers to get personalized training insights and analyze their performance through simple conversations with Google’s AI assistant.
The new integration lets users connect their Strava accounts directly to Gemini and ask questions about their activity history, training progress, and performance across different sports. The move follows Strava’s recent integration with Anthropic’s Claude .
Once connected, Gemini can analyze activity trends to answer questions such as whether a runner is getting faster at the same heart rate, how strength training affects their running performance, or how they performed in their most recent race. Users can also ask for a mile-by-mile breakdown of their race efforts.
Moreover, Gemini can also compare a user’s fastest 10K time this year against their all-time best, track current and longest activity streaks across sports, and examine how weather conditions may have affected a workout.
For instance, users can ask Gemini how much heat slowed them down during a particular run. The assistant can factor in temperature, humidity, wind, and other conditions recorded alongside the activity to provide a more contextual analysis.
Strava’s Gemini integration is optional and read-only. So while the AI assistant can access activity information, it can’t modify a user’s Strava account. Users also have the option to disconnect the service at any time.
Strava’s Gemini integration is now rolling out in the US and is available to subscribers across all Gemini plans. To get started, users need to open Personal Intelligence in Gemini , select Strava under connected apps, sign in, and authorize access to their account.
There is no word yet on availability in other markets.
